info.name: AgroStore — Agri Cold Storage Booking API
info.description:
Backend API for AgroStore, a cold-storage booking platform for Bangladeshi farmers.

Farmers reserve cold-storage capacity by the kilogram for a date window, pay storage rent through Stripe, have the lot quality-graded at intake, and settle a recalculated bill on withdrawal.

## Roles

| Role | What they do |
|---|---|
| `FARMER` | Search warehouses, check availability, book capacity, pay, withdraw, review |
| `WAREHOUSE_OWNER` | Register warehouses and chambers, approve bookings, store and release lots |
| `ADMIN` | Approve warehouses, grade intake quality, manage users, refunds, audit logs |

## Getting started

1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (defaults to `http://localhost:8000`).
2. Run **Auth → Login** with one of the demo accounts. The test script stores `accessToken` automatically, and every other request inherits it.
3. Requests that are public (crop types, warehouse search, availability, reviews) are set to **No Auth** and work without logging in.

## Response envelope

Success: `{ "success": true, "message": "...", "data": {...}, "meta": {...} }`

Error: `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errors": [ { "path": "...", "message": "..." } ] }`

`meta` appears only on paginated lists. `errors` only on failures.

## Status codes used

`400` validation · `401` bad credentials or token · `403` wrong role or not your record · `404` not found · `409` conflict or illegal state transition · `410` OTP expired · `422` business rule violated · `429` rate limited · `502` upstream (email/Stripe) failed

request.description: Plain-text liveness check. Returns `server running....`

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Signup, email verification by OTP, login with rotating refresh tokens, Google sign-in, and password management.

**Verification is enforced before login.** A new account must submit the OTP emailed at signup; until then login returns `403`.

request.description:
Creates the account and emails a 6-digit OTP. **No tokens are returned** — the user must verify before logging in.

`role` accepts only `FARMER` or `WAREHOUSE_OWNER`. Sending `ADMIN` returns `400`; admin accounts can only be created by promoting an existing user.

Unknown fields are rejected, so `status` or `role: ADMIN` cannot be smuggled in.

request.description:
Uses the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie Postman stored at login — send an empty body.

Issues a brand-new pair and **revokes the old refresh token**, so replaying it returns `401`. The user is re-read from the database, so a banned or deleted account cannot refresh even with a previously valid token.

If you are not using cookies, pass `{ "refreshToken": "..." }` explicitly.

Adds the session's `jti` to a Redis denylist until it would have expired.

Access and refresh tokens of a session share one `jti`, so this kills **both immediately** — the access token does not stay usable for its remaining 15 minutes. Idempotent: always `200`.

For accounts created through Google, which have no password yet. Afterwards the user can sign in **either** way.

Returns `409` if the account already has a password — use Change Password instead.
Requires the current password. Returns `409` on a Google-only account (no password set) — use Set Password instead.

request.description:
Redirects (302) to the Google consent screen. **Open this in a browser**, not in Postman.

Google accounts are always created as `FARMER` and are auto email-verified — no OTP needed, since Google already proved ownership of the address. Warehouse owners and admins are refused with `403`.

An existing farmer who signed up with a password gets their `googleId` linked to the same account rather than a duplicate.

The flow uses a CSRF `state` value stored in Redis with a 5-minute TTL, deleted on use.

`GET /warehouses` returns **APPROVED only**. Owners see their own pending ones through `GET /warehouses/me`.

Public search with filtering, sorting and pagination.

The `cropTypeId` filter is the interesting one — it reads the crop's ideal temperature range and returns only warehouses with a chamber that can actually hold it. That is the same rule the booking engine enforces, surfaced as a filter.

An unknown `sortBy` is rejected with `400` rather than silently ignored — the whitelist prevents sorting by arbitrary columns.

item.name: Bookings
item.description:
The core of the platform.

## Lifecycle

```
PENDING_APPROVAL ──approve──► APPROVED ──pay──► PAID ──store──► STORED
       │                          │                                │
       ├─reject─► REJECTED        ├─hold lapses─► EXPIRED          ▼
       └─cancel─► CANCELLED       └─cancel─► CANCELLED     WITHDRAW_REQUESTED
                                                                   │
                                                                   ▼
                                                              COMPLETED
```

Every illegal jump returns `409` naming the states you *can* move to. `COMPLETED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED` and `EXPIRED` are final.

## Capacity

Creating a booking takes a **row lock on the chamber** inside a transaction, recomputes the peak committed load across overlapping date ranges, and only then inserts. Two farmers claiming the last 500 kg simultaneously produce one `201` and one `409` — never two bookings.

request.description:
FARMER only. Rules enforced, in order:

1. `startDate` not in the past, at most 90 days ahead
2. Chamber active, warehouse `APPROVED`
3. **Crop temperature must fit inside the chamber's range** — `422` otherwise
4. Duration at least the warehouse's `minBookingDays`
5. Duration at most the crop's `maxStorageDays`
6. **Quantity within peak free capacity for the window** — `409` otherwise, inside a row-locked transaction

request.description: FARMER only. Returns the caller's own bookings.
Visible to the farmer who owns it, the owner of the warehouse holding it, or an admin. Anyone else gets `403`.

Full cost breakdown: quantity, rate, booked days, the minimum-booking floor, actual days stored, the settlement (base cost, overstay days, surcharge), the payment record, and the outstanding balance.

Once a booking is `COMPLETED`, the `finalCost` recorded at completion is authoritative — the invoice does not silently recompute it.

WAREHOUSE_OWNER only, own warehouse only.

Sets a **30-minute payment hold** (`holdExpiresAt`). An unpaid hold that lapses stops counting against chamber capacity and the booking becomes `EXPIRED` — handled lazily at read time, so no cron job is needed.

response.name: 409 — illegal transition

request.description: WAREHOUSE_OWNER only. `reason` is optional and stored on the booking.
FARMER only, own booking only. Allowed while `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `APPROVED` or `PAID`. A cancelled `PAID` booking needs an admin refund.

WAREHOUSE_OWNER only. Requires the booking to be `PAID`.

Refused with `409` if the intake inspection graded the lot `REJECTED` — a failed lot cannot be stored, it must be refunded.
FARMER only, own lot only. Moves `STORED` → `WITHDRAW_REQUESTED`.

WAREHOUSE_OWNER only. Confirms release and **computes the final cost**:

```
billableDays = max(actualDaysStored, minBookingDays)
baseCost     = quantityKg × rate × billableDays
overstayDays = max(0, actualDays − bookedDays)
surcharge    = quantityKg × rate × overstayDays × 0.5
finalCost    = baseCost + surcharge
```

So an early withdrawal still pays the minimum-days floor, and an overstay pays 1.5× on the extra days.

item.name: Inspections
item.description:
Admins grade produce quality at intake, between payment and storage.

A grade of `REJECTED` **cancels the booking in the same transaction** and flags it for refund — one call, two consistent writes.

request.description:
ADMIN only. The booking must be `PAID` — inspection happens at intake, before storage.

`grade` is `A`, `B`, `C` or `REJECTED`. One inspection per booking.

**`REJECTED` auto-cancels the booking** with reason "Failed intake quality inspection", and `store` will then refuse the lot.

response.name: 201 — grade REJECTED cancels the booking

request.description: ADMIN only.
Visible to the admin, the farmer whose lot it is, and the warehouse owner holding it — the involved parties. Anyone else gets `403`.

item.name: Payments
item.description:
Stripe Checkout. Storage rent is priced in **BDT** and charged in **USD** at a documented `DEMO_FX_RATE`, because the Stripe test account is USD-only. Both amounts and the rate are stored on the payment row, so an invoice is reconstructable.

## The important rule

**Only the signature-verified webhook may mark a booking `PAID`.** The success redirect merely reads status — a user typing that URL cannot pay for themselves. If the webhook secret is not configured the endpoint returns `503` rather than trusting an unverifiable event.

exec: console.log('Open this URL to pay: ' + body.data.checkoutUrl);

request.description:
FARMER only, own booking only. The booking must be `APPROVED` and its hold must not have expired.

Open the returned `checkoutUrl` in a browser and pay with the Stripe test card **4242 4242 4242 4242**, any future expiry, any CVC.

response.name: 201 Created
409 — booking not APPROVED

header.description: Generated by Stripe. A forged or missing signature returns 400.

request.description:
**Not called by hand** — Stripe calls it. Listed here for documentation.

Registered with `express.raw()` **before** `express.json()`, because signature verification needs the untouched request body.

Handles `checkout.session.completed` (→ Payment `SUCCEEDED`, Booking `PAID`), `checkout.session.expired` and `payment_intent.payment_failed`.

**Idempotent** — Stripe retries deliveries. The update is `WHERE status = 'PENDING'`, so a duplicate matches zero rows and writes nothing.

Local testing:
```
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/api/v1/payments/webhook
```

Where Stripe redirects after payment. **Read-only** — it reports status and never mutates anything.

If the webhook has not landed yet it says so and asks you to refresh, rather than pretending the booking is paid.
Where Stripe redirects if the farmer abandons checkout. The booking stays held until its hold expires.
FARMER only.
The farmer who made it, or an admin. Anyone else gets `403`.

ADMIN only. Calls the Stripe Refund API, then marks the payment `REFUNDED` and writes an audit row.

Only a `SUCCEEDED` payment can be refunded; a second attempt returns `409`.

item.name: Reviews
item.description:
A farmer may review a warehouse once, and only after the booking is `COMPLETED`.

The warehouse's `avgRating` and `reviewCount` are **denormalized and recomputed inside the same transaction** as every create, edit and delete — so the rating can never drift from the reviews, and the warehouse list can sort by rating without aggregating on every request.

request.description: Public, paginated.

FARMER only, own booking only, and the booking must be `COMPLETED` — otherwise `409`.

`rating` is 1 to 5. One review per booking.

response.name: 409 — booking not completed

request.description: FARMER only, own review only. Recomputes the warehouse rating.
The farmer who wrote it, or an admin moderating. **Soft delete**, and the warehouse rating is recomputed.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Platform administration.

**Guards worth knowing:** an admin cannot modify their own account, and cannot modify another admin — otherwise one mis-click could lock everyone out of the platform. Role changes are blocked when they would orphan data.

Every status and role change writes an `AuditLog` row **inside the same transaction** as the change, so an audit entry can never exist for a rolled-back write.

request.description: ADMIN only. Soft-deleted accounts are hidden unless `includeDeleted=true`.
ADMIN only. Full record including both profile types and related counts.

ADMIN only. `status` is `ACTIVE` or `BANNED`.

Banning takes effect **immediately** — the account cannot log in and cannot refresh an existing token, because the auth middleware re-reads the user from the database on every request.

Returns `403` if the target is your own account or another admin.

ADMIN only. **This is the only way to create an ADMIN** — signup refuses that role outright.

Blocked with `409` if the change would orphan data: an owner who still owns warehouses, or a farmer with active bookings.

response.name: 409 — would orphan warehouses

request.description:
ADMIN only. `PENDING` | `APPROVED` | `REJECTED` | `SUSPENDED`.

A warehouse must be `APPROVED` before it appears in public search or accepts bookings.
ADMIN only. Platform-wide booking list.
ADMIN only. Every row carries before/after snapshots, the acting admin, and the IP.

item.name: Error Handling
item.description: Every error uses the same envelope. These requests are here so the behaviour is documented and reproducible.

request.description: Unmatched paths fall through to a 404 handler registered just before the global error handler.
